text:
maria: quick check — in the console mockups i pushed this morning i tightened the CTA group spacing on dashboard cards. need a fast decision because eng wants to lock the card layout for the sprint.

sam: saw it, looks denser. can you call out the token changes? how does this affect touch targets?

maria: good call. current tokens: `--space-3` horizontal, `--space-2` vertical. proposal: reduce horizontal to `--space-2` (8px) and keep vertical at `--space-2` so buttons sit closer. touch target still >=44px tall.

linh: @maria can you paste the exact CSS? will affect our flex-gap fallback. also, how does it behave at 320px width?

maria: sure — example:```css
.button-group { display:flex; gap: var(--space-2); }
.button { padding: calc(var(--space-2) / 1) var(--space-2); }
```shrinks nicely, we cap min-width on primary at 96px so labels don't wrap weirdly.

alex: visually it's tighter and feels more modern. my only worry: the ghost/secondary buttons look cramped next to primary when label lengths vary. could we use `button--compact` variant for short actions only?

maria: yes — `button--compact` for icon + short-label only. otherwise default button stays a little wider.

eva: accessibility nits: make sure compressed horizontal spacing doesn't drop the focus ring visual contrast. also keyboard focus order must remain logical when buttons wrap — prefer single-row collapse to vertical stack (primary first).

linh: on wrap we currently reverse the DOM order for mobile to push primary to top — that was causing focus surprises. proposal: keep DOM order same, use CSS `order` only for visual placement but not for focus. folks okay?

alex: i prefer keeping DOM order intact. simpler and less surprising for screen readers.

eva: agree. also for toasts — noticed stacking in the console overlays: newest message currently appended to bottom and pushes others up. that's odd for discoverability. can we have newest on top and prefer to auto-dismiss older ones? aria-live should be `polite` for non-critical toasts.

maria: proposal for toasts: newest on top, max stack 3, auto-dismiss timeline 6s for info, 12s for warnings, persistent for errors. `aria-live: polite` unless `role=alert` for error.

sam: sounds reasonable. how do we handle overlapping toasts with the new denser CTA groups? potential collision on small cards in the right rail.

linh: we can offset toast container with `--space-4` from the right rail and set `pointer-events: none` on the container then `pointer-events: auto` on toast itself — prevents accidental clicks on underlying UI.

maria: noted. also add a small visual separation token `--toast-gap: var(--space-2)` so stacked toasts don't look glued to CTA chips.

alex: tiny copy thing — dismiss label on toasts should be `Dismiss` not `Close` for consistency with buttons.

maria: done. I'll update the spec doc and add a small accessibility checklist: focus ring contrast, DOM order preserved, aria-live rules, keyboard dismiss (Esc), focus restoration to the triggering element.

eva: add a test case for screen readers: announce sequence when two toasts appear in quick succession. we should verify NVDA/JAWS behavior.

design-bot: deploy-preview for `card-layout-v3` available at https://deploy-preview/redwood/cards/v3 — visual diffs + token changes included.

sam: thumbs up from PM side. if eng + a11y are good, we can freeze for the sprint.

linh: will try the branch today, will flag any regressions by EOD.

maria: thanks all — i'll push the token PR and update the console components doc. :pray:
